key_insight: RSM–Rao-3–TOPSIS optimization identified 110–121 A peak current and 28–33 Hz pulsing for full penetration of 3.0 mm Ti-6Al-4V plate with narrower weld beads and heat-affected zones.
engineering_relevance: The optimized settings offer a route to full single-pass penetration while limiting bead width and heat-affected-zone size compared with fully penetrated welds at 160 A.
method: Conducted 20 bead-on-plate experiments spanning 100–160 A peak current and 1–50 Hz pulse frequency.
Built second-order response surface models for bead width, penetration depth, and heat-affected-zone width.
Generated Pareto solutions with parameter-free Rao-3 optimization and selected compromises using TOPSIS across ten weight sets.
evidence_signal: The models showed mean prediction errors below 2.7%; optimized full-penetration solutions had 28–35% narrower beads and 17–33% narrower heat-affected zones than fully penetrated welds at 160 A.
watch_item: Results derive from 20 bead-on-plate experiments on 3.0 mm plate; transfer to production joints, other thicknesses, and mechanical-property requirements needs validation.
paper_title: Multi-objective optimization of pulsed tungsten inert gas welding process parameters for Ti-6Al-4 V alloy using response surface methodology, Rao-3 algorithm, and TOPSIS
